_comment: Canary: gmail credential  (watcher objective gmail-healthy, infra-objectives/objectives)
Proves that n8n's Gmail OAuth credential works, and NOTHING else. The watcher on the DreamHost
VPS calls it hourly; DreamHost has root on that box, so the token it holds must not amount to
access to the mailbox. Hence: no input is read from the request, the Gmail call is fixed (list
labels), and the response carries only a count — no label names, no message data.
Same credential ('Gmail account') as 'Query: gmail search', the email-todo and the parking
connectors, so it fails exactly when they do. On 2026-10-03 that credential died at 13:00 UTC
(a 7-day Testing-mode expiry, ADR 0008) and took down the invoice approval gate unnoticed.
The Gmail error is caught on the node's error output and answered as 503 {ok:false}, so the
watcher can tell 'the credential is broken' (503 with a body) from 'n8n is down' (no answer,
or Traefik's 502). An UNHANDLED failure (n8n's own 500) means the canary itself is broken.
JSON rather than @n8n/workflow-sdk TypeScript like its neighbours: deployed through n8n's public
REST API from infra-objectives (agent.env N8N_API_*), not the MCP tooling. Credentials are
referenced by NAME; the deploy step resolves names to ids, so this file holds no id and no
secret. 'Watcher gmail canary' is a Header Auth credential (header X-Canary-Token) created by
the owner, with the same value as op://watcher/n8n-gmail-canary/token.
Successful executions are not saved (one an hour, all identical); failed ones are, so a
failure can be read in n8n afterwards.
name: Canary: gmail credential

parameters.responseBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ ok: false, error: String(($json.error && ($json.error.message || $json.error.description)) || 'gmail call failed').slice(0, 300) }) }}
